# Form

Collects, validates and submits data. Fields go in `Form.Item`, `Form.useForm()` returns the form instance and
`Form.List` manages fields that are added and removed dynamically. Fields are validated on blur, and submitting
scrolls to and focuses the first invalid field.

**Interaction**: a field is validated on blur and does not interrupt typing; once it has shown an error, it is
validated on every change, so the error disappears as soon as it is corrected; errors appear below the field.
Submitting validates all fields, then scrolls to and focuses the first invalid one. When `validateTrigger` is set
on Form or Form.Item, validation follows it instead.

**Category**: Basic · **Common uses**: Create and edit dialogs, settings pages, sign-in

## Import

```ts
import { Form } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

Put fields in `Form.Item` and declare validation with `rules`; on submit, `onFinish` receives the values of all
fields.

```tsx
export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Form layout="vertical" onFinish={() => {}}>
      <Form.Item
        label="Project name"
        name="name"
        rules={[{ required: true, message: 'Enter a name' }]}
      >
        <Input placeholder="For example: Website redesign" />
      </Form.Item>
      <Form.Item label="Visibility" name="visibility" initialValue="team">
        <Select
          options={[
            { value: 'team', label: 'Team only' },
            { value: 'public', label: 'Public' },
          ]}
        />
      </Form.Item>
      <Form.Item label="Notifications" name="notify" valuePropName="checked" initialValue>
        <Switch />
      </Form.Item>
      <Button type="primary" htmlType="submit">
        Save
      </Button>
    </Form>
  )
}
```

## Advanced

### Form instance

`Form.useForm()` returns an instance that validates and submits the form from outside, such as the confirm
button of a dialog.

```tsx
export function WithInstance() {
  const [form] = Form.useForm<{ title: string }>()
  return (
    <Form form={form} layout="vertical">
      <Form.Item
        label="Task name"
        name="title"
        rules={[{ required: true, message: 'Enter a task name' }]}
      >
        <Input />
      </Form.Item>
      <Inline>
        <Button type="primary" onClick={() => form.submit()}>
          Submit
        </Button>
        <Button onClick={() => form.resetFields()}>Reset</Button>
      </Inline>
    </Form>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Contents of the form: Form.Item fields, the submit button and so on. | — | No |

Also accepts the props of the corresponding Ant Design component (`FormProps`), except `style` and `className`.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
